cells.tense: You are pulling the loose threads together into a shape that holds, and the pulling is yours.
cells.ask: At the next choice, name the option you are pulling for before you weigh the rest, and let that stand.
cells.core: You are the one pulling the loose threads together into something that holds. You do not force a shape onto them — you wait until they line up, then you name what you see. That is why what you say lands clean.\n\nA quiet sense of what is fair moves with it, and you lean on that sense rather than on a tally. What you give and what comes back stay roughly even without much scorekeeping. Looking over the whole, you are reading a verdict off the arrangement rather than hunting for one. Where this is bent right now: it runs unnamed, so it goes unchecked. Say it once in your own words and it becomes something you can stand behind.
cells.sheetLine: You see where this is pointing before you can prove it.

cells.tense: You are assembling the whole thing before it arrives, and the arriving keeps getting pushed back.
cells.ask: Pick one thing and move on it today. Not the best one. The next one in front of you.
cells.core: You are already ahead, assembling a version of this that has not happened yet. Every angle gets checked, every loose piece gets forced into place. The gathering keeps expanding and the moment you were gathering for has moved past.\n\nThe cost is that direction gets decided in the head instead of felt. What is moving underneath has opinions — real ones — and they cannot reach the surface. So the momentum runs tight instead of steady. Action does not need the whole plan. One step taken from what is already yours to carry beats the perfect arrangement of things you cannot hold yet.
cells.sheetLine: You are solving it before it has arrived.

cells.tense: You are standing at a door that closed behind you, still working out what happened in that room.
cells.ask: Tell one person how you actually felt about something you have been carrying. Not the story. One sentence.
cells.core: The pieces are scattered and you are not gathering them. You are back at a moment that wants collecting, feeling around for what should have been done, while the room has moved on. What you do next stays pointed at what already happened.\n\nThe felt sense of what is fair has gone quiet. What is left is a habit of waiting to see how it lands before you decide what you feel. Nothing gets named, so nothing settles. What charges this back up is not more thinking — it is sitting with one thing you can feel in your body. A recognition that does not have to be argued. Let that be what you gather, and the rest starts moving on its own.
cells.sheetLine: You are waiting for the room to settle before you know how you feel.

cells.tense: You are already gathering the pattern into a whole, though you call what you are doing something more ordinary.
cells.ask: Tell someone one thing you have seen that holds. Not what is wrong with it. What has held.
cells.core: The gathering is running. You are the one who sees what connects across the table, what the scattered parts add up to — and you have been calling that your job, or being perceptive, or just paying attention. It gets done in plain sight.\n\nWhat keeps it unclaimed is that it feels too simple to name. It arrives as observation, not as something you did. Sharing one piece of it — not to prove anything, just to pass it on — puts the whole thing back where it came from. Simple, direct, no accounting needed. That is where this kind of seeing belongs, and that is what it does when you let it move between people.
cells.sheetLine: You are already seeing the whole thing. You call it something else.
